come_follow_me.title: “Seek the Lord, and Ye Shall Live”
come_follow_me.summary: Jonah ran the other way, yet the Lord didn’t give up on him, on Nineveh, or on us. He keeps sending prophets with this message: because of Jesus Christ, it’s not too late to change, and He will offer another chance.
questions: What conclusions can we draw when a prophet prophesies? (Amos 3:1–8)
How has seeking the Lord brought you life? (Amos 5:4, 14–15)
How do you know when you are spiritually hungry? (Amos 8:11–12)
What do you learn from Jonah that can help you be more merciful? (Jonah 3–4)

daily.quote: the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets
daily.thought: God shows His love by sending prophets. What is something a prophet has taught that has helped you?

daily.quote: Seek ye me, and ye shall live
daily.thought: Seeking the Lord brings life and joy. What is one way you can seek Him today?

daily.quote: a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord
daily.thought: We need God’s word like we need food. When do you feel most hungry for it?

daily.quote: saviours shall come up on mount Zion
daily.thought: Doing temple work for others is a small way to help like the Savior. How could our family take part?

daily.quote: God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way
daily.thought: The Lord is merciful to all who turn to Him. Who can you show mercy to this weekend?

daily.quote: thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness
daily.thought: Jonah knew who God really is. What words would you use to describe His mercy?

daily.quote: Seek good, and not evil, that ye may live
daily.thought: Choosing good leads to life. What good choice can you make this week?

deep_dive.intro: Jonah sailed away from the job God gave him, and a great storm followed. But the Lord hadn’t given up on Jonah, on the people of Nineveh, or on any of us. He keeps sending prophets with this message: if we repent, we will not be cast off forever, because of Jesus Christ it’s not too late to change.

scripture_blocks.about: The Lord reveals truth through His prophets
Seek the Lord, and ye shall live
A famine of hearing the words of the Lord
The Lord is merciful to all who turn to Him

principles.title: The Lord reveals truth through His prophets.
principles.explain: Just like a roaring lion means there is prey nearby, a prophet speaking means God has spoken. Having prophets is a way God shows He loves us and tells us what we need to know.

principles.title: “Seek the Lord, and ye shall live.”
principles.explain: When hard things happen, God hopes we will turn to Him. Looking for Him in our daily lives brings real joy and life.

principles.title: The word of the Lord can satisfy spiritual hunger and thirst.
principles.explain: Without God’s word, we’d feel spiritually hungry, like having no food. The Restoration of the gospel ended that famine, and reading the scriptures fills us up.

principles.title: Who are the “saviours … on mount Zion”?
principles.explain: When we do temple work for people who have died, we help them in a small way like the Savior helps us.

principles.title: The Lord is merciful to all who turn to Him.
principles.explain: Jonah ran away, was swallowed by a great fish, and then obeyed. The people of Nineveh turned to God and He forgave them. Jonah was upset, but God wanted him to learn mercy too.

key_verses.text: Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.
For thus saith the Lord unto the house of Israel, Seek ye me, and ye shall live:
Behold, the days come, saith the Lord God, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord:
And God saw their works, that they turned from their evil way; and God repented of the evil, that he had said that he would do unto them; and he did it not.

And he prayed unto the Lord, and said, I pray thee, O Lord, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.

quote.text: having prophets is a sign of God’s love
quote.by: Elder Ulisses Soares, “Prophets Speak by the Power of the Holy Spirit,” Ensign or Liahona, May 2018, 99

questions: What conclusions can we draw when a prophet prophesies? What else do you learn about prophets from Amos 7:10–15?
What has the Lord revealed to you through His prophets?

How do you know when you are spiritually hungry? (Amos 8:11–12)
What do you learn from Jonah that can help you be more merciful?

activity.title: Prophets are messengers
activity.steps: Whisper a simple message to one person and ask them to pass it to the others. How is the messenger like a prophet? Why does the Lord give us prophets? Then sing “Follow the Prophet” (Children’s Songbook, 110–11), and share why you choose to follow God’s prophet. Bonus: write out Amos 3:7, then cover a few words at a time until everyone can say it from memory.

scripture.text: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.

deep_dive.intro: Your Heavenly Father is a God of truth. All truth comes from Him and leads to Him. You show that you value truth when you keep learning, live with integrity, and bravely stand for what you know is right.

teachings.title: Always be learning
teachings.explain: Heavenly Father wants His children to keep learning—at school, in training, and from sources you trust. Education isn’t just about money; it’s part of becoming more like Him. Ask the Lord to guide you.

teachings.title: Learn spiritual truths
teachings.explain: While you learn about the world, learn about the Savior who created it. Seminary and personal gospel study help you know Him and prepare to serve a mission and share the gospel.

teachings.title: Live with integrity
teachings.explain: Integrity means loving what is right more than being comfortable or popular. Don’t steal, lie, cheat, or deceive—at school, at work, or online. Be the same person when no one is watching.

teachings.title: You have something precious to share
teachings.explain: The gospel holds answers to life’s questions. You don’t have to know everything—you know enough to love your neighbor, share true principles, and invite friends to learn more.

teachings.title: Questions can build faith
teachings.explain: Having questions isn’t weakness. Joseph Smith was 14 when he asked a question with faith. Look for answers in the scriptures, the prophets, family, leaders, and God—and keep living what you already know.

quotes: Living with integrity means you love what is right in the sight of God—more than you love personal comfort, popularity, or convenience. It means doing what is right simply because it is right.
Be the same faithful follower of Jesus Christ in public and in private.
When you stand up for the teachings of Jesus Christ, He stands with you. Jesus Christ is your strength!
deep_dive.blessings: Education increases your ability to serve the Lord, including as a missionary. It empowers you to bless others, especially your family. The more you learn, the more you can help build God’s kingdom and influence the world for good.
questions: Why does God want you to learn about Him and the world around you?
What should you do when you have questions?
Do you strive to be honest in all that you do?
Am I the same follower of Jesus Christ online and in private as I am at church?
How can I stand up for what is right without being unkind to people who believe differently?
